page: Microsoft Azure E64ads_v5 is a memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. It features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance provides 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a 2,577 GB solid-state drive, while graphics processing units are absent.

Benchmark measurements show high performance across memory-bound and parallel computational tasks. The system achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score of 2,978.82 and delivered 63.59 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. Parallel throughput is demonstrated by a multi-core Geekbench score of 17,837.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 294.47 GB/sec. Large uncached memory bandwidth registers at 124.14 GB/sec for reads and 62.31 GB/sec for writes. Single-core performance falls in the mid-range tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,720.0.

Without discrete accelerators, large-parameter machine learning generation is constrained, achieving 2.67 tokens per second on 70B models. The combination of dense memory allocation, dedicated AMD cores, and integrated fast NVMe storage provides balanced efficiency for large enterprise databases, in-memory caches, large-scale Clang compilation jobs, and high-concurrency data processing workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E64ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs from a 32-core AMD EPYC 7763 processor alongside 512.0 GB of RAM. Configured with an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and 2,577 GB of local SSD storage, the instance is engineered for memory-intensive enterprise tasks without discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark results confirm robust multi-threaded and memory subsystems, evidenced by a PassMark memory score of 2,978.82, Redis throughput exceeding 63.59 million operations per second, and strong software compilation throughput under Clang. Uncached sequential memory bandwidth and single-thread execution place in the median tier across comparable hardware, while 70B model inference exhibits CPU-bound limitations. The instance provides high resource density and local cache performance suitable for large in-memory databases, distributed caches, data analytics pipelines, and batch compilation workloads.
